# Test cases based on the specific rules:
# 1. Tabs expanded (default 8)
# 2. Each whitespace character becomes one space
# 3. Runs are NOT collapsed (multiple spaces stay multiple spaces)
# 4. Whitespace at line breaks dropped (except leading whitespace of whole text)
# 5. Words longer than width ARE broken
# 6. Result is a list of lines none longer than width (unless forced)

# Case 1: Basic wrapping and tab expansion
assert wrap_("Word1 Word2\tWord3", 8) == ["Word1 Word2", "Word3"], (wrap_("Word1 Word2\tWord3", 8), ["Word1 Word2", "Word3"])

# Case 2: Runs are NOT collapsed (multiple spaces preserved)
assert wrap_("Word1  Word2", 10) == ["Word1  Word2"], (wrap_("Word1  Word2", 10), ["Word1  Word2"])

# Case 3: Whitespace at line breaks dropped (leading whitespace of whole text kept)
# "  Line1\n  Line2" -> "  Line1" and "Line2"
assert wrap_("  Line1\n  Line2", 10) == ["  Line1", "Line2"], (wrap_("  Line1\n  Line2", 10), ["  Line1", "Line2"])

# Case 4: Words longer than width are broken
assert wrap_("Supercalifragilistic", 5) == ["Super", "calif", "ragil", "istic"], (wrap_("Supercalifragilistic", 5), ["Super", "calif", "ragil", "istic"])

# Case 5: Word exactly at width
assert wrap_("Word1 Word2", 6) == ["Word1 ", "Word2"], (wrap_("Word1 Word2", 6), ["Word1 ", "Word2"])

# Case 6: Complex mix - tabs, multiple spaces, and long words
# "A\tB  C\n D" -> "A B  C" (Line 1) -> "D" (Line 2)
# "A B  C" is length 6. If width is 5: ["A B", " C"]? 
# Wait, "A B  C" with width 5: "A B" (len 3), then "  C" (len 3). 
# Since "  C" doesn't fit after "A B", it moves to next line.
assert wrap_("A\tB  C\n D", 5) == ["A B", " C", "D"], (wrap_("A\tB  C\n D", 5), ["A B", " C", "D"])

# Case 7: Leading whitespace of whole text preserved, but trailing whitespace of lines dropped
# "  Word1 \n Word2" -> "  Word1" and "Word2"
assert wrap_("  Word1 \n Word2", 10) == ["  Word1", "Word2"], (wrap_("  Word1 \n Word2", 10), ["  Word1", "Word2"])

# Case 8: Single unbreakable chunk forcing width (Rule: none longer than width except where forced)
# If a word is 10 chars and width is 5, it breaks. 
# If the rule meant "unbreakable" as in no spaces, my function breaks them.
# The prompt says "words longer than width ARE broken", so there are no "unbreakable" chunks.
assert wrap_("LongWord", 3) == ["Lon", "gWo", "rd"], (wrap_("LongWord", 3), ["Lon", "gWo", "rd"])

# Case 9: Multiple newlines
# "Line1\n\nLine2" -> "Line1" and "Line2" (because \n\n results in an empty line which is stripped)
assert wrap_("Line1\n\nLine2", 10) == ["Line1", "Line2"], (wrap_("Line1\n\nLine2", 10), ["Line1", "Line2"])

def wrap_(text, width):
    # 1. Expand tabs (default 8)
    text = text.expandtabs()
    
    # 2. Handle line breaks: split into lines
    raw_lines = text.splitlines()
    if not raw_lines:
        return []
        
    processed_lines = []
    for i, line in enumerate(raw_lines):
        if i == 0:
            # Keep leading whitespace of the whole text
            processed_lines.append(line)
        else:
            # Drop leading and trailing whitespace of subsequent lines
            processed_lines.append(line.strip())
    
    # Join with a single space to represent the "dropped" newline whitespace
    # This creates a continuous stream where newlines are replaced by a space
    combined = " ".join(processed_lines)
    
    # 3. Process character by character to respect "runs are NOT collapsed"
    # and "each whitespace character becomes one space" (already handled by join/strip)
    res = []
    current_line = ""
    
    i = 0
    while i < len(combined):
        char = combined[i]
        
        if char.isspace():
            # If we can fit the space, add it
            if len(current_line) + 1 <= width:
                current_line += " "
                i += 1
            else:
                # Cannot fit the space, finish current line
                if current_line:
                    res.append(current_line)
                current_line = " " # Start new line with the space
                i += 1
        else:
            # It's a non-space character (part of a word)
            # Find the end of this word
            j = i
            while j < len(combined) and not combined[j].isspace():
                j += 1
            word = combined[i:j]
            
            if len(current_line) + len(word) <= width:
                current_line += word
                i = j
            else:
                # Word doesn't fit in current line
                if not current_line:
                    # Word is longer than width and we are at start of a line
                    # Break the word into chunks of 'width'
                    for k in range(0, len(word), width):
                        chunk = word[k:k+width]
                        res.append(chunk)
                    i = j
                else:
                    # Current line has content, finish it and try word again
                    res.append(current_line)
                    current_line = ""
                    # Do not increment i, re-process word in next loop
                    
    if current_line:
        res.append(current_line)
        
    # Final cleanup: remove any empty strings and strip trailing whitespace 
    # from lines (as per "whitespace at line break is dropped")
    final = []
    for line in res:
        stripped = line.rstrip()
        if stripped:
            final.append(stripped)
            
    return final
